citations.claim: energy exceeds allowed at first violation step 25
post-bounce upward speed inflated vs pre-bounce

counterfactual.change: changed bodies[0].e from 1.0 to 0.9 only; this adds dissipation on bounce so collision no longer gains net energy and energy_bound is not violated

explanation: Single ball dropped from y=3.4 hits floor between step 24-25 with e=1. With large dt~0.0308 and 8 substeps, the impulse + positional correction on floor collision adds energy: speed magnitude increases from 7.25 (pre-bounce, step24) to 8.62 (post-bounce, step25) instead of conserving, raising total energy from ~32.95 to 42.34, exceeding allowed 41.689. Lowering e to 0.9 removes net gain, proving restitution handling at large dt is cause.
vision_note: A single blue ball falls under gravity toward the floor over steps 22 to 24 and is in contact with the floor at step 25, the claimed violation step. No other bodies, walls, or controller waypoints are visible, and there is no tunneling through the floor, only a floor impact event.
